rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲧⲱⲃϩ̄ 'pray, beseech, exhort, intercede, advocate' (regular Lyc. ⲥ for ϩ). Used both nominally and verbally throughout this page. The cosmic Mother of Life intercedes for the First Man at her consummation; the Church likewise intercedes for departing catechumens. Captures the prayer-on-behalf-of dimension that fits both registers. Cf. accumulated ⲧⲧⲱⲃⲍ 'I beseech.'

Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲁⲏ 'end, last' with prosthetic ϣ- and -ⲁ ending — possibly a Manichaean technical term for the cosmic moment of completion/consummation. Recurs three times on this page in the formula 'at the ⲡϣⲁⲏⲁ they did X' marking decisive cosmic moments (giving glory, intercession). Translated 'consummation' to capture the end-as-fulfillment sense.

Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲟⲱⲃ. Possibly related to ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲟⲃⲉ 'the abomination/foul thing' (accumulated vocab). Paired antithetically with ⲡⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'destruction' as the dual register of the cosmic prison into which the First Man descends. Captures the moral-cosmological negation.

Tentatively read as Lycopolitan variant of Sahidic ⲥⲱϣⲛϩ 'labor, distress, struggle' (Crum). With preceding [ⲥⲁ-]: 'after toil/labor unto eternity' — fits the eschatological rest-after-struggle topos that pervades Manichaean soteriology.

Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ⲣ̄- (verbal prefix) + ⲥⲙ̄ⲙⲉ ('steer, govern'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Cf. accumulated ⲣ̄ⲍⲙ̄ⲙⲉ 'to steer.' Used here for the First Man as 'steerer of all the works of the multitude.'

Substantival from ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲧⲛ 'be wide, spread' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲉⲥⲧⲁⲛⲧ qualitative 'wide/broad'). Used in soteriological register: 'to give him wideness/room forth from this all' = to grant cosmic release/freedom. Pair-partner with the verbs of release in the Manichaean soteriological lexicon.

proposed_english: the Father in him / the indwelling Father
rationale: ⲙⲙⲁϩ = Lyc. locative 'in him' (= ⲙ̄ⲙⲟϥ in some uses). The phrase names the Father-presence indwelling the First Man — a Manichaean theological motif where the Mother's intercession effects the indwelling of the Father in the First Man. Distinguished from agentive uses of ⲡⲓⲱⲧ as separate cosmological figure.
